title: Special events
subtitle: a festival is held, takes place, lasts, consists of
summary: Describe festivals and celebrations: when they are held, how long they last, and what they consist of.

lesson.heading: A fireworks display
lesson.text: The Sydney **fireworks display** (a show for people to watch) is **held** (organised) every year. More than a million people **gather** (come together) at the **harbour** on New Year's Eve to **celebrate** the new year.

examples.text: The display is **held** every year on New Year's Eve.
A **harbour** is an area of water where ships are safe from the sea.

lesson.heading: Words for describing an event
rows: a show for people to watch
do something enjoyable on a special day
be included in an event or activity
move around as part of a group, often to celebrate (also a noun)

lesson.heading: An arts festival
lesson.text: The Edinburgh Festival is an **annual** event (it happens once a year). It **consists of** at least six different festivals which **take place** in the city and **last** for almost six weeks. The most **popular** one has **up to** 500 performances a day.

examples.text: The festivals **take place** across the city.

lesson.heading: The Chinese Spring Festival
lesson.text: The Spring Festival is the biggest traditional festival in China. The day before it starts, people from **all over** China return to their family homes. The next day many people **dress up**, and children receive money in red envelopes.

examples.text: Many people **dress up** for the festival.
Another popular **custom** is to put poems on the gates.

lesson.heading: custom and tradition

left.label: a custom
left.text: Something that people usually do. The adjective is **customary**.
examples: It is **customary** to take your shoes off before you enter a mosque.

right.label: a tradition
right.text: A very old custom that has continued for a long time. The adjective is **traditional**.
examples: It is **traditional** to give each other presents.
We went to a **traditional Greek wedding**.

lesson.note: Word order: a traditional Greek wedding, not a Greek traditional wedding.

lesson.text: An event *takes place*, but people *hold* it: The festival takes place in August. The festival is held in August.

exercises.prompt: Match each word with its meaning.

pairs.right: a show for people to watch
an area of water where ships are safe
move round the streets in a group

exercises.prompt: If you are involved in an activity, you are ___ in it.
exercises.explanation: To be involved in an event means to be included in it.

exercises.prompt: The theatre can hold up to 25 people. What does this mean?
exercises.explanation: up to 25 = 25 is the maximum number.

exercises.prompt: A harbour is a place where ___ are kept.
exercises.explanation: A harbour is an area of water where ships are kept safe from the sea.

exercises.prompt: The children wear special clothes for the festival. = The children ___ for the festival.
People come from everywhere in Japan. = People come from ___ Japan.
exercises.explanation: all over Japan = everywhere in Japan.

exercises.prompt: They hold the event every year. = The event ___ every year.
exercises.explanation: An event that people organise every year is held every year.

exercises.prompt: The festival happens every year. = The festival is an ___ event.
The Fallas ___ for five days and finishes on March 19th.
exercises.explanation: last = continue for a period of time.

exercises.prompt: The festival ___ of music, dancing, cooking and parades.
Every day crowds ___ in different parts of the city at 2 pm.
exercises.explanation: gather = come together in one place.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the right order. (The festival happens in the summer.)
exercises.answer: The festival takes place in the summer

exercises.statement: We went to a Greek traditional wedding last year.
exercises.explanation: We went to a traditional Greek wedding last year. The adjective traditional comes before the nationality.
